eToro review 2026 is it safe – that’s the question many traders ask as they consider joining one of the most talked‑about social trading platforms. In this article we’ll walk through the latest updates, regulatory standing, security features, and overall user experience to help you decide whether eToro remains a trustworthy choice in 2026.

## eToro Overview 2026
eToro has evolved from a simple copy‑trading site into a multi‑asset broker offering stocks, ETFs, crypto, commodities, and CFDs. By 2026 the platform boasts over 30 million registered users worldwide, with a refreshed interface that emphasizes mobile‑first design and AI‑driven portfolio suggestions. The core appeal still lies in its social feed, where you can follow top performers and automatically mirror their trades. Despite the growth, the company maintains its headquarters in Cyprus and retains operational hubs in the UK, US, and Australia, which influences its regulatory footprint.

## Regulation & Licensing
Safety starts with oversight, and eToro holds licenses from several reputable authorities. In Europe it is regulated by the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) under license number 109/10. For UK clients, eToro UK Ltd is authorized by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) under reference 583263. Australian traders fall under the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) license 491139. In the United States, eToro USA LLC is registered with the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) and operates as a broker‑dealer under SEC oversight. These multiple registrations mean the platform must meet strict capital adequacy, reporting, and client‑protection standards in each jurisdiction.

## Safety & Security Features
Beyond licenses, eToro employs a layered security approach. All client funds are kept in segregated accounts at top‑tier banks, ensuring they are not used for the company’s operational expenses. The platform uses TLS 1.2 encryption for data in transit and AES‑256 encryption for data at rest. Two‑factor authentication (2FA) is mandatory for login and withdrawal requests, and biometric login options are available on mobile apps. eToro also runs regular penetration tests and maintains a bug‑bounty program to encourage ethical hackers to report vulnerabilities. In 2026 the platform added real‑time fraud monitoring powered by machine learning, which flags anomalous trading patterns before they can cause harm.

## Account Protection
eToro provides negative balance protection for retail clients in the EU, UK, and Australia, meaning you cannot lose more than your deposited amount when trading CFDs. For non‑leveraged stock and ETF purchases, your assets are held directly in your name through a custodian, reducing counterparty risk. The platform also offers an insurance policy via Lloyd’s of London that covers up to €1 million per client against fraud or insolvency of the broker, subject to terms and conditions. These safeguards aim to give traders peace of mind, especially when markets become volatile.

## Trading Instruments & Fees
The breadth of instruments has expanded: you can now trade over 2 500 stocks, 150 ETFs, 40+ cryptocurrencies, and a variety of commodities and indices. eToro’s fee structure remains competitive. Stock and ETF trades are commission‑free for most regions, with a small spread applied.
